svg.text: E-C Kolbenrohr — everything is a pipe
An open dairy tube with a loose piston is the universal vessel: it cuts, doses, forms, kneads — and is cleaned as a pipe.
torpedo CIP: 5.5 L · 0.3 kWh · 6–7 min per tube
Zone F ≈ 0.5 m² per meal (smallest of the four)
SECTION, 1 px per mm (holster gaps drawn ×3 wider)
flow must pass every mm²: no spray shadow
grid end plate on the mouth
Knead / mix: two tubes nose to nose, closed, no dust
Push to form and dose: the tube is a syringe

g.text: butter dosed by stroke, no scoop
All plates are loose, held only by the station's clamping force: no fastener anywhere.
Grids are the one shape that traps fibres: reverse jets, bread pig, camera check.

svg.text: 1/6 Fill: the loose piston is the floor; the box tilts potatoes into the upright tube on a load cell
2/6 A dicing-grid end plate is laid on the mouth; the gantry flips the tube into the cutting yoke
3/6 Ram pushes the piston: the grid cuts sticks, the sickle below cuts them to length — dice fall into the pot
4/6 Pig: the piston scrapes the bore empty; piston and plate go to the small-parts rack
5/6 Torpedo holster: tube slid over a fixed core; wash water forced through 3 mm gaps at 1.5 m/s
6/6 A camera looks down the bore and sees the whole food surface in one image
